changesets.summary: Client journeys and a performance gate
changesets.details:
- Every instruction now has one ordered journey on a live Surfnet through the generated Rust client (`every_instruction_runs_in_one_journey`) and through the generated TypeScript client (`typescript_client_runs_every_instruction`), which the Rust side drives with funded fixtures and then checks the resulting on-chain state. The TypeScript journey asserts the client's PDA helpers reproduce the Rust-derived addresses before sending anything.
- The journey's keypairs are seeded, so identical binaries measure identical compute units.
- A `performance` workflow benchmarks the pull request against its base: deployed binary size plus every instruction's compute units (median of three journey runs), posted as one consolidated PR comment. The policy fails the check on any binary-size increase or a compute-unit regression above 2%, unless the pull request carries `performance-approved`. `scripts/benchmark.ts` and `scripts/compare-benchmarks.ts` run the same pipeline locally.
- `docs/performance.md` documents the pipeline and the policy.

review_request.title: test(pina_amm): drive every instruction through each client and gate performance
test(pina_amm): drive every instruction through each client and gate performance

changesets.summary: Choose the most you will pay or the least you will receive
changesets.details:
##### User impact

Swaps, deposits, and withdrawals now require absolute token limits that you choose. The RPC's simulation results can no longer weaken those limits. Replace `--slippage-bps` with `--minimum-out` or `--maximum-in` for swaps, and both `--maximum-amount-0/1` or `--minimum-amount-0/1` values for liquidity. Verify prices independently before choosing your limits; quotes remain advisory.

review_request.title: fix(cli)!: require explicit swap and liquidity limits
fix(cli)!: require explicit swap and liquidity limits

changesets.summary: Require explicit absolute CLI limits
changesets.details: Replace simulation-derived slippage bounds with required caller-provided minimum output or maximum input for swaps and two explicit token limits for deposits and withdrawals. Remove `--slippage-bps`; keep swap quotes advisory and reject events describing another swap. Command results report submitted limits rather than simulated execution amounts.

review_request.title: fix(cli)!: require explicit swap and liquidity limits
fix(cli)!: require explicit swap and liquidity limits

changesets.summary: Keep average prices accurate in pools with extreme ratios
changesets.details:
##### User impact

Average prices now retain the entire elapsed price history even when one token is much scarcer than the other. A continuously positive pool price can no longer appear to be zero because its accumulator ran out of room, and swaps continue to settle.

review_request.title: fix(oracle)!: preserve the full TWAP integral
fix(oracle)!: preserve the full TWAP integral

changesets.summary: Preserve the full time-weighted price integral
changesets.details: The canonical price accumulator in `Pool` and `PoolSynced` now combines `price_0_cumulative_last` (low) with `price_0_cumulative_high_last` (high) into a 256-bit value. All generated clients expose both limbs. Integrators must reconstruct the full value before subtracting samples; every supported reserve ratio and timestamp window has a delta below `2^192`, so the complete integral is recoverable without halting trading. Take both samples after migration, which initializes the high limb to zero and cannot recover previously lost cycles.

review_request.title: fix(oracle)!: preserve the full TWAP integral
fix(oracle)!: preserve the full TWAP integral

changesets.summary: Test-only hardening: exact-rounding proofs, mutation gaps, invariant fuzzing
changesets.details:
No program behavior changes; the `patch` bump is what the changeset API classification asks for a test-module edit inside the program package.

The math module's tests now pin the exact rounding of every quoted amount by cross-multiplication — fees as exact ceilings, outputs as exact floors, shares as exact floors — closing the coverage gaps a first cargo-mutants run surfaced: exact-output fee amounts were never checked numerically, the constant-product guard's rejection path was never exercised, and the zero-sided liquidity amounts were untested. A seeded Surfpool fuzzer additionally drives one pool through random swap, deposit, withdraw, sync, and collection sequences, asserting the security model's global invariants after every transaction, and an extreme-ratio pool now proves end to end that trading continues after the accumulator wraps.

review_request.title: test: close mutation gaps, prove exact rounding, and fuzz the invariants
test: close mutation gaps, prove exact rounding, and fuzz the invariants

changesets.summary: The AMM has its permanent mainnet address
changesets.details:
##### User impact

The AMM now lives at `pAMMzVPRwtrxQs2CjLTUUpfCAp9XdvVmwwVhpAuCobi`. Pools, fee tiers, and liquidity tokens are created under this address, so wallets and apps should use the latest clients to find them.

review_request.title: chore(pina_amm)!: deploy under the mainnet identity pAMMzVPRwtrxQs2CjLTUUpfCAp9XdvVmwwVhpAuCobi
chore(pina_amm)!: deploy under the mainnet identity pAMMzVPRwtrxQs2CjLTUUpfCAp9XdvVmwwVhpAuCobi

changesets.summary: Deploy under the mainnet program identity
changesets.details:
The program's address moves from `pAMMvXaqR2VVFqznf6dgvUFQjLXXAEeL9cb48cXsGeV` to `pAMMzVPRwtrxQs2CjLTUUpfCAp9XdvVmwwVhpAuCobi` before its first mainnet deployment.

- `declare_id!` was synced with `pina keys sync`, and `pina migrations create` rebound the unpublished migration history (no publication receipts existed) to the new ID.
- The TypeScript, Dart, Rust, and CPI clients were regenerated: `PINA_AMM_PROGRAM_ADDRESS`, `PINA_AMM_ID`, the event source address, and every PDA helper's default program address now name the new ID, so every config, pool, LP mint, and vault PDA changes with it.
- Integrators that hard-code the old ID, or CPI callers that pin an older `pina_amm_cpi`, must update before calling the deployed program.

review_request.title: chore(pina_amm)!: deploy under the mainnet identity pAMMzVPRwtrxQs2CjLTUUpfCAp9XdvVmwwVhpAuCobi
chore(pina_amm)!: deploy under the mainnet identity pAMMzVPRwtrxQs2CjLTUUpfCAp9XdvVmwwVhpAuCobi

changesets.summary: Pools can no longer name an empty creator address
changesets.details:
##### User impact

Fees that would have accrued to an address nobody controls are now impossible to create: naming the unset default address as a pool creator fails with `DefaultCreator`, and so does handing an existing pool's creator rights to it.

review_request.title: fix(pina_amm): reject the default address as a pool creator
fix(pina_amm): reject the default address as a pool creator

changesets.summary: Reject the default address as a pool creator
changesets.details: `CreatePool` and `SetPoolCreator` reject the default address with the new `DefaultCreator` error. Creator fees accrued to the default address could never be collected, yet they still reduce the reserves every withdrawal pays from.

review_request.title: fix(pina_amm): reject the default address as a pool creator
fix(pina_amm): reject the default address as a pool creator

changesets.summary: Read RPC failures safely
changesets.details:
##### User impact

RPC errors and failed simulation logs show terminal control characters as visible text, so an endpoint cannot use diagnostics to erase terminal output or manipulate the clipboard. Scripts using `--json` can read command failures as an `error` object on stderr.

review_request.title: fix(cli): escape terminal controls in command errors
fix(cli): escape terminal controls in command errors

changesets.summary: Escape terminal controls in CLI diagnostics
changesets.details: Neutralize control characters in every command error at the stderr rendering boundary, including failed simulation logs and RPC errors. Under `--json`, command errors emit one JSON object on stderr with an `error` string.

review_request.title: fix(cli): escape terminal controls in command errors
fix(cli): escape terminal controls in command errors

changesets.summary: A slightly cheaper, slightly smaller program
changesets.details:
##### User impact

Swaps, deposits, and withdrawals each cost 10–25 fewer compute units, and the deployed program is about 0.5 KB smaller, which lowers its rent. Every processor now builds the pool PDA's signer through one shared helper instead of a compiled copy per call site. Nothing about the math, fees, or account layout changed.

review_request.title: perf(pina_amm): share one pool-signer seed builder across processors
perf(pina_amm): share one pool-signer seed builder across processors

changesets.summary: Trim the deployed program and every instruction's compute
changesets.details: Compiles the pool PDA's signer-seed builder once instead of a copy per call site: the deployed binary shrinks by 520 bytes and swaps, deposits, and withdrawals each get slightly cheaper. No account, instruction, event, or wire format changes.

review_request.title: perf(pina_amm): share one pool-signer seed builder across processors
perf(pina_amm): share one pool-signer seed builder across processors

changesets.summary: Pools now track their average price over time
changesets.details:
##### User impact

Every market now keeps a running sum of its price over time, and a new permissionless `SyncPool` instruction advances it on demand. Anyone can sample that sum at two moments to compute a time-weighted average price that a single transaction cannot meaningfully move — the standard building block for pricing collateral and rewards. Nothing else about trading changes: swaps cost the same and advance the accumulator themselves.

review_request.title: feat(pina_amm): add a time-weighted price accumulator and admin events
feat(pina_amm): add a time-weighted price accumulator and admin events

changesets.summary: Time-weighted price accumulator and admin events
changesets.details:
- Every pool now sums its price over time: `price_0_cumulative_last` (Q64.64 price of token 1 in token 0, times seconds) advances on every swap with the pre-trade price and on the new permissionless `SyncPool` instruction. Sample it twice and divide by the elapsed time for a manipulation-resistant average, exactly like Uniswap V2; see `docs/math.md`.
- `UpdateConfig` emits `ConfigUpdated` and `SetPoolCreator` emits `PoolCreatorChanged`, so indexers can follow tier-rate and fee-recipient changes without polling accounts.
- `SyncPool` emits `PoolSynced` with the reserves and the accumulator after the advance.
- `Pool` grows two fields; `pina migrations create` recorded the automatic transition and the generated clients, IDL, and ABI layout test are regenerated.

review_request.title: feat(pina_amm): add a time-weighted price accumulator and admin events
feat(pina_amm): add a time-weighted price accumulator and admin events

changesets.summary: Wrap the price accumulator instead of halting the pool
changesets.details: `advance_price_accumulator` now wraps modulo `2^128`, like Uniswap V2, instead of failing with `MathOverflow`. The accumulator only ever grows, so a checked sum would have failed every swap and `SyncPool` permanently once a pool with an extreme price ratio had accumulated enough time, with no way to recover short of a program upgrade. Integrators must subtract samples with wrapping arithmetic; `docs/math.md` shows how. The function no longer returns a `Result`.

review_request.title: fix(pina_amm): wrap the price accumulator instead of halting the pool
fix(pina_amm): wrap the price accumulator instead of halting the pool

changesets.summary: Average prices can no longer be rewritten after the fact
changesets.details:
##### User impact

A pool's time-weighted average price now only counts each price for the time it actually stood. Sending tokens straight into a pool and syncing it can no longer change the average for time that has already passed, so integrations that rely on the average are much harder to manipulate. New fee tiers now announce themselves with an event, and the program publishes its security contact details so researchers can reach the maintainers privately.

review_request.title: fix(pina_amm): price the TWAP accumulator with stored reserves
fix(pina_amm): price the TWAP accumulator with stored reserves

changesets.summary: Price the accumulator with stored reserves so donations cannot reprice the past
changesets.details:
The time-weighted price accumulator priced the whole interval since `last_update_timestamp` with the reserves read from the vaults _now_. Reserves are vault balances, so a donation straight to a vault followed by `SyncPool` or a swap in the same transaction repriced time that had already passed; with flash-deposited liquidity (deposits and withdrawals are feeless) the attacker recovered nearly all of the donation.

- `Pool` gains `reserve_0_last` and `reserve_1_last`, the reserves at the last observation. `CreatePool`, both swaps, `Deposit`, `Withdraw`, and `SyncPool` now accrue the elapsed interval with those stored reserves first, then store their own post-instruction reserves, exactly like Uniswap V2's `_update`. Deposits and withdrawals now advance the accumulator too.
- The new pure `PriceOracle::observe` holds the logic; property tests prove the accumulator equals the per-second integral of the observed reserves across mixed swaps, deposits, withdrawals, donations, and syncs.
- `docs/math.md` and `docs/security.md` describe the sampling rules and the remaining limits honestly: the average resists single-transaction manipulation, not a price held across seconds.
- `CreateConfig` emits the new `ConfigCreated` event with the tier's index, rates, authority, and pool-creator restriction.
- The deployed binary embeds a `security.txt` pointing at `SECURITY.md` and the private advisory form.

review_request.title: fix(pina_amm): price the TWAP accumulator with stored reserves
fix(pina_amm): price the TWAP accumulator with stored reserves

changesets.summary: Safely preview transactions
changesets.details:
##### User impact

Quotes and simulation previews no longer send your signature to the RPC service. The service cannot turn a preview into a trade or another action on your behalf.

review_request.title: fix(cli): keep quote and simulation transactions unsigned
fix(cli): keep quote and simulation transactions unsigned

changesets.summary: Keep simulation transactions unsigned
changesets.details: Construct quote and `--simulate` transactions with placeholder signatures and a default blockhash. Fetch a recent blockhash and sign only when sending a transaction, so an RPC cannot broadcast a captured simulation with the user's authority.

review_request.title: fix(cli): keep quote and simulation transactions unsigned
fix(cli): keep quote and simulation transactions unsigned

#### Test-only hardening: exact-rounding proofs, mutation gaps, invariant fuzzing

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #29](https://github.com/pina-rs/amm/pull/29)

No program behavior changes; the `patch` bump is what the changeset API classification asks for a test-module edit inside the program package.

The math module's tests now pin the exact rounding of every quoted amount by cross-multiplication — fees as exact ceilings, outputs as exact floors, shares as exact floors — closing the coverage gaps a first cargo-mutants run surfaced: exact-output fee amounts were never checked numerically, the constant-product guard's rejection path was never exercised, and the zero-sided liquidity amounts were untested. A seeded Surfpool fuzzer additionally drives one pool through random swap, deposit, withdraw, sync, and collection sequences, asserting the security model's global invariants after every transaction, and an extreme-ratio pool now proves end to end that trading continues after the accumulator wraps.

- **Escape terminal controls in CLI diagnostics.** Neutralize control characters in every command error at the stderr rendering boundary, including failed simulation logs and RPC errors. Under `--json`, command errors emit one JSON object on stderr with an `error` string.
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #35](https://github.com/pina-rs/amm/pull/35)
- **Trim the deployed program and every instruction's compute.** Compiles the pool PDA's signer-seed builder once instead of a copy per call site: the deployed binary shrinks by 520 bytes and swaps, deposits, and withdrawals each get slightly cheaper. No account, instruction, event, or wire format changes.
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #15](https://github.com/pina-rs/amm/pull/15)
- **Keep simulation transactions unsigned.** Construct quote and `--simulate` transactions with placeholder signatures and a default blockhash. Fetch a recent blockhash and sign only when sending a transaction, so an RPC cannot broadcast a captured simulation with the user's authority.
  _Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #32](https://github.com/pina-rs/amm/pull/32)

sections.title: What's new
entries:
#### Choose the most you will pay or the least you will receive

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #34](https://github.com/pina-rs/amm/pull/34)

##### User impact

Swaps, deposits, and withdrawals now require absolute token limits that you choose. The RPC's simulation results can no longer weaken those limits. Replace `--slippage-bps` with `--minimum-out` or `--maximum-in` for swaps, and both `--maximum-amount-0/1` or `--minimum-amount-0/1` values for liquidity. Verify prices independently before choosing your limits; quotes remain advisory.

#### Keep average prices accurate in pools with extreme ratios

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #33](https://github.com/pina-rs/amm/pull/33)

##### User impact

Average prices now retain the entire elapsed price history even when one token is much scarcer than the other. A continuously positive pool price can no longer appear to be zero because its accumulator ran out of room, and swaps continue to settle.

#### The AMM has its permanent mainnet address

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #19](https://github.com/pina-rs/amm/pull/19)

##### User impact

The AMM now lives at `pAMMzVPRwtrxQs2CjLTUUpfCAp9XdvVmwwVhpAuCobi`. Pools, fee tiers, and liquidity tokens are created under this address, so wallets and apps should use the latest clients to find them.

#### Pools can no longer name an empty creator address

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #9](https://github.com/pina-rs/amm/pull/9)

##### User impact

Fees that would have accrued to an address nobody controls are now impossible to create: naming the unset default address as a pool creator fails with `DefaultCreator`, and so does handing an existing pool's creator rights to it.

#### Read RPC failures safely

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #35](https://github.com/pina-rs/amm/pull/35)

##### User impact

RPC errors and failed simulation logs show terminal control characters as visible text, so an endpoint cannot use diagnostics to erase terminal output or manipulate the clipboard. Scripts using `--json` can read command failures as an `error` object on stderr.

#### A slightly cheaper, slightly smaller program

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #15](https://github.com/pina-rs/amm/pull/15)

##### User impact

Swaps, deposits, and withdrawals each cost 10–25 fewer compute units, and the deployed program is about 0.5 KB smaller, which lowers its rent. Every processor now builds the pool PDA's signer through one shared helper instead of a compiled copy per call site. Nothing about the math, fees, or account layout changed.

#### Pools now track their average price over time

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #10](https://github.com/pina-rs/amm/pull/10)

##### User impact

Every market now keeps a running sum of its price over time, and a new permissionless `SyncPool` instruction advances it on demand. Anyone can sample that sum at two moments to compute a time-weighted average price that a single transaction cannot meaningfully move — the standard building block for pricing collateral and rewards. Nothing else about trading changes: swaps cost the same and advance the accumulator themselves.

#### Average prices can no longer be rewritten after the fact

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #18](https://github.com/pina-rs/amm/pull/18)

##### User impact

A pool's time-weighted average price now only counts each price for the time it actually stood. Sending tokens straight into a pool and syncing it can no longer change the average for time that has already passed, so integrations that rely on the average are much harder to manipulate. New fee tiers now announce themselves with an event, and the program publishes its security contact details so researchers can reach the maintainers privately.

#### Safely preview transactions

_Owner:_ [@ifiokjr](https://github.com/ifiokjr) · _Review:_ [PR #32](https://github.com/pina-rs/amm/pull/32)

##### User impact

Quotes and simulation previews no longer send your signature to the RPC service. The service cannot turn a preview into a trade or another action on your behalf.
